# Audette IT — full site content

> Every page of audetteit.com in one file, for AI agents and anyone who wants plain text. Generated from the per-page Markdown files; the HTML pages are the canonical versions.

## How this site serves Markdown

- Each page has a Markdown twin: `/` is `/index.md`, `/services` is `/services.md`, and so on.
- Requesting any page URL with `Accept: text/markdown` returns the same Markdown with `Content-Type: text/markdown`. Those responses send `Vary: Accept`.
- Markdown responses carry a `Link: <...>; rel="canonical"` header pointing at the HTML page.
- Index of pages: https://audetteit.com/llms.txt
- XML sitemap: https://audetteit.com/sitemap.xml

## Audette IT

> Tech help from one person in Las Vegas: everyday fixes like wifi, slow computers, printers and TVs, plus network design, Active Directory and self-hosted services. In person around Las Vegas, or remotely from anywhere.

### Tech help for every room in your house

I'm Michael. I fix the everyday stuff like wifi, slow computers, printers and TVs, and I can build the serious stuff too.

- [Get in touch](https://audetteit.com/contact.md)
- [See what I help with](https://audetteit.com/services.md)

In person around Las Vegas, or remotely from anywhere.

#### Room by room

- **Living room:** TV and streaming. Smart TVs, streaming boxes, sound bars, and getting everything onto the right input without three remotes.
- **Kitchen:** smart home. Smart speakers, doorbells, cameras, and the plugs and lights that stopped responding.
- **Office:** the computer and printer. Slow computers, new computer setup, backups, and printers that won't print.
- **Kids' room:** parental controls. Screen time and content filtering on their devices, plus filtering at the router that covers the whole house.
- **Hall closet:** the router. Wifi that reaches the back bedroom, a network that doesn't drop during calls, and a router that's actually set up securely.
- **Garage:** the deeper stuff. Network design, a small server or home lab, self-hosted services, and Active Directory when you need it.

### What I help with

Most of what I do is the everyday stuff. When you need more than that, I can design and build the kind of setup most homes never get.

**Around the house:** Wifi and devices, Slow computers, New computer setup, Backups, Printers, TVs and smart home, Accounts and software, Parental controls.

**The deeper stuff:** Network design, Active Directory, Self-hosted services, Security hardening.

[More about each of these](https://audetteit.com/services.md)

### How it works

No tickets and no call center. You talk to me from start to finish.

1. **Tell me what's going on.** Send a quick email or use the contact form. What's broken, or what you want set up, is enough to start.
2. **I figure out the fix.** I'll reply with what I think is wrong and a quote. Then we pick a time, in person or remote.
3. **It works, and you know why.** I fix it and explain what I did in plain English, so it's less of a mystery next time.

[Questions people ask](https://audetteit.com/how-it-works.md)

### Who you're dealing with

Just me, Michael. Not a company and not a call center. The person you email is the person who fixes it.

- **Where:** In person around Las Vegas, or remotely from anywhere.
- **Devices:** Computers and laptops, inside and out. Phones and tablets for setup, settings and parental controls, but no physical repairs.
- **Cost:** Every job is different, so I'll give you a quote before I start.

### Something acting up?

Tell me what's going on. I'll get back to you with what I think it is and what it'd take to fix. Email michael.audette@audetteit.com or use the [contact form](https://audetteit.com/contact.md).

## What I help with

> Two kinds of help. The everyday fixes that come up in every house, and bigger projects most family tech support can't take on.

### Around the house

- **Wifi and devices:** Dead spots, dropped connections, and things that won't connect.
- **Slow computers:** Finding what's actually slowing it down, then fixing that.
- **New computer setup:** Getting it ready and moving your stuff over from the old one.
- **Backups:** So your photos and files survive a dead drive.
- **Printers:** Getting printers and scanners talking to everything again.
- **TVs and smart home:** Streaming, smart TVs, speakers, cameras and the rest.
- **Accounts and software:** Locked-out accounts and settings that stopped making sense.
- **Parental controls:** Screen time and filtering on the kids' devices and the home network.

### The deeper stuff

- **Network design:** Planning a home or small-office network properly, from the router out.
- **Active Directory:** Domains, user accounts and group policy, set up the right way.
- **Self-hosted services:** Running your own media, backups and tools on hardware you own.
- **Security hardening:** Firewalls, access control and closing the gaps default setups leave open.

### Not sure which one your problem is?

You don't need to know. Just tell me what's happening.

- **Where:** In person around Las Vegas, or remotely from anywhere.
- **Devices:** Computers and laptops, inside and out. Phones and tablets for setup, settings and parental controls, but no physical repairs.
- **Cost:** Every job is different, so I'll give you a quote before I start.

### Something acting up?

Tell me what's going on. I'll get back to you with what I think it is and what it'd take to fix. Email michael.audette@audetteit.com or use the [contact form](https://audetteit.com/contact.md).

## How it works

> No tickets and no call center. You talk to me from the first email to the fix.

1. **Tell me what's going on.** Send a quick email or use the contact form. What's broken, or what you want set up, is enough to start.
2. **I figure out the fix.** I'll reply with what I think is wrong and a quote. Then we pick a time, in person or remote.
3. **It works, and you know why.** I fix it and explain what I did in plain English, so it's less of a mystery next time.

### In person or remote, whichever fits

If you're around Las Vegas, I can come to you. That's usually best for wifi coverage, printers, TVs and anything that needs hands on the hardware.

A lot of problems can also be fixed remotely, wherever you are. That works well for slow computers, accounts, software and settings.

### Questions people ask

If yours isn't here, just email me.

#### Do you come to the house?

Yes, around Las Vegas. A lot of things can also be fixed remotely, wherever you are.

#### Can you help remotely?

Yes. Plenty of problems, like slow computers, accounts, software and settings, can be sorted out over a remote connection.

#### Do you fix phones and tablets?

I help with setup, settings, apps and parental controls on them. I don't do physical repairs like screens or batteries.

#### What about computers and laptops?

Yes, Windows or Mac, including hardware work like swapping a drive or adding memory.

#### How much does it cost?

It depends on the job, so I'll give you a quote before I start anything.

#### Is it only for big projects?

No. Most of what I do is everyday stuff like wifi, printers and slow computers. The bigger projects are there when you need them.

### Something acting up?

Tell me what's going on. I'll get back to you with what I think it is and what it'd take to fix. Email michael.audette@audetteit.com or use the [contact form](https://audetteit.com/contact.md).

### Contact form

The form at https://audetteit.com/contact asks for:

- **Name**
- **Email**
- **What's going on?**
- A checkbox: "I'm okay with this info being used to follow up with me." (see the [privacy note](https://audetteit.com/privacy.md))

This opens your email app with the message filled in. Nothing is sent until you hit send there. Emailing the address above directly works just as well.

## What this site collects

> Short version: very little, and nothing is sold or shared.

### The contact form

The form on the [contact page](https://audetteit.com/contact.md) doesn't send anything to a server. When you hit send, it opens your own email app with your name, email, and message filled in. Nothing leaves your device until you send that email yourself. Once it arrives, I use it only to reply to you.

### Analytics and cookies

The site uses Google Analytics, loaded through Google Tag Manager, to count visits and see which pages get used. Tag Manager loads on every page, but **analytics cookies are only set if you click "Accept" on the cookie banner.**

Until you accept (or if you decline), Google Analytics runs in a restricted mode: no cookies, no identifiers stored on your device. Google can still receive basic, cookieless signals, like that a page was viewed, with the time and general browser details, which it uses for aggregate counts.

If you accept, Google Analytics sets its own cookies (named `_ga` and `_ga_…`) and sends Google things like the pages you view, roughly where you are, and what device and browser you're using. Google handles that under [Google's privacy policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). It's used only to see how the site is doing. It isn't used for ads, and I don't combine it with anything else.

The site also uses **Microsoft Clarity**, loaded through Tag Manager, to see how pages are used: clicks, scrolling, and anonymized recordings of page visits, which help find layout problems. What you type into form fields is masked and never recorded. Clarity follows the same banner choice. Until you accept, it runs without cookies and treats every page view as a separate visit. If you accept, it sets its own cookies (`_clck`, `_clsk`) so visits can be linked across pages. Microsoft handles that data under the [Microsoft Privacy Statement](https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement). It isn't used for ads.

Your choice is remembered in your browser's local storage (not a cookie), so the banner doesn't ask on every page. You can change it any time with **cookie settings** at the bottom of every page. Declining after accepting clears the analytics cookies from both.

### Hosting

The site is hosted on Cloudflare, which processes standard request data (like IP addresses) to serve and protect the site. That's covered by [Cloudflare's privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/).

Fonts load from Google Fonts, so your browser also makes a request to Google's servers when a page loads. Google Fonts doesn't set cookies; see [Google's Fonts privacy FAQ](https://developers.google.com/fonts/faq/privacy).

### Questions

Email michael.audette@audetteit.com if you want to know what I have from you, or want it deleted.
